destination.title: Black-hole corrections, thermodynamics and adjoining structures
destination.question: How do specified gravitational and matter corrections change black-hole thermodynamics, extremality and geometry, and which variational, duality and holographic descriptions apply?
destination.summary: The strongest core concerns corrected black-hole equilibria and their calculation. Geometry, dualities, holography, nonlinear matter and quantum near-extremality provide related questions without establishing equivalence. No verbal scope accompanied the original numerical region, so its membership is assessed as a research neighborhood rather than an accepted scientific classification.

systems: Charged, rotating and scalar-coupled black holes in the source-specific gravitational theories
String effective theories, selected higher-curvature models and nonlinear or nonminimal matter theories
Adjacent duality, holographic and quantum near-extremal descriptions
targets: Thermodynamic quantities, entropy prescriptions and extremality relations
Corrected solutions, horizon regularity and validity of approximations
Conditional consistency bounds and source-specific microscopic comparisons
regimes: Dimensions, asymptotics, charge sectors and rotation restrictions remain source-specific
Leading perturbation theory, nonlinear truncated actions and all-orders model constructions remain distinct
Extremal, near-extremal and non-extremal questions are all eligible
assumptions: No universal positivity, thermodynamic stability, supersymmetry or UV-completion premise
Numerical membership and source-selection labels provide provenance, not scientific validation
conventions: Held-fixed variables, boundary data and renormalization schemes must accompany thermodynamic comparisons
Euclidean-action extremalization is distinct from zero-temperature black-hole extremality
includes: Useful alternate homes for questions outside the thermodynamic correction core
excludes: Treating the collection as one fine question
A universal entropy-increase or weak-gravity theorem
Treating type II compactification targets as black-hole thermodynamic premises

sources.title: Higher Derivative Corrections to R-charged Black Holes: Boundary Counterterms and the Mass-Charge Relation

evidence.text: Can curvature-squared Einstein–Maxwell theory be holographically renormalized with a perturbatively well-defined variational principle, and how do its corrections affect charged black-hole thermodynamics, extremal mass/charge ratios and proposed weak-gravity/viscosity connections?

sources.title: Kerr-Newman Black Holes with String Corrections

evidence.text: Do Kerr-Newman and more general Einstein-Maxwell solutions survive a supersymmetric four-derivative correction, and can their corrected entropy be controlled continuously from BPS to Schwarzschild limits?

sources.title: Leading higher-derivative corrections to Kerr geometry

evidence.text: What effective theory captures the leading higher-derivative deformations of four-dimensional vacuum GR black holes, including scalar-controlled couplings, and how do its rotating solutions modify Kerr horizon geometry, thermodynamic quantities, photon rings and scalar profiles?

sources.title: Higher derivative corrections to Kerr black hole thermodynamics

evidence.text: How do six- and eight-derivative gravitational EFT operators change Kerr thermodynamics at first order, can those changes be obtained without the corrected metric, and when do entropy corrections have definite signs?

sources.title: T-duality equivalences beyond string theory

evidence.text: Does corrected T-duality preserve non-extremal black-hole horizons, entropy and temperature throughout a two-parameter family of four-derivative theories, including parameter choices without a known string-theory origin?

sources.title: On the extremality bound of stringy black holes

evidence.text: How do first-order heterotic α′ corrections change the extremal charge-to-mass ratio of explicitly embedded, nonsupersymmetric dyonic black holes, and do those changes track corrections to Wald entropy?

sources.title: $\alpha'$ corrections of Reissner-Nordström black holes

evidence.text: What are the complete first-order α′ corrections to a specified non-extremal dyonic RN embedding in heterotic string theory, and what do its thermodynamics imply about proposed links between entropy shifts, extremality and the WGC?

sources.title: Electromagnetic Quasitopological Gravities

evidence.text: Can nonminimal curvature–electromagnetic couplings extend generalized quasitopological gravity while retaining single-function charged spherical solutions, tractable thermodynamics, and nonperturbative information about regularity and extremality?

sources.title: D = 5 rotating black holes in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity: mass and angular momentum in extremality

evidence.text: How do perturbative quadratic-curvature corrections change the extremal mass–angular-momentum relation and entropy of five-dimensional rotating black holes, and how should extremality be approached when non-extremality is itself of the coupling's order?

sources.title: Duality-invariant extensions of Einstein-Maxwell theory

evidence.text: Which higher-derivative Einstein–Maxwell theories preserve electromagnetic duality with non-minimal curvature couplings, how much can field redefinitions simplify them, and what black-hole constraints follow?

sources.title: Exact electromagnetic duality with nonminimal couplings

evidence.text: Can nonminimal curvature couplings quadratic in the electromagnetic field strength be completed to exact electromagnetic duality, and what are the resulting charged black-hole and extremal near-horizon properties?

sources.title: String gravity in D=4

evidence.text: What minimal four-dimensional gravitational theory follows from heterotic string theory at first order in α′, and how does it modify neutral Kerr geometry, thermodynamics and potentially the extremal spin bound?

sources.title: Non-supersymmetric black holes with α′ corrections

evidence.text: How do first-order heterotic α′ corrections depend on the relative signs of extremal black-hole charges, and what do the corrected masses, entropies and T-duality properties imply for nonsupersymmetric branches?

sources.title: Corrections to AdS$_{5}$ black hole thermodynamics from higher-derivative supergravity

evidence.text: How do supersymmetric four-derivative corrections change charged, rotating AdS5 black-hole thermodynamics, and do the corrected action and BPS entropy match the dual superconformal index?

sources.title: Negative corrections to black hole entropy from string theory

evidence.text: Must leading higher-derivative corrections increase black-hole entropy at fixed conserved quantities when the uncorrected configuration is thermodynamically stable and the relevant Wilson coefficients arise at tree level? The paper tests this proposed positivity condition using rotating string solutions.

sources.title: Effectiveness of Weyl gravity in probing quantum corrections to AdS black holes

evidence.text: Can field redefinitions into a Weyl-tensor basis simplify leading higher-curvature corrections to rotating AdS black-hole thermodynamics, including all three curvature-squared invariants of five-dimensional minimal gauged supergravity?

sources.title: Quadratic curvature correction and its breakdown to thermodynamics of rotating black holes

evidence.text: What are the leading quadratic-curvature corrections to Myers–Perry thermodynamics in different ensembles, where do they diverge, and do these divergences necessarily survive beyond perturbation theory?

sources.title: Black Hole Solutions with Electric and Magnetic Charges in Nonlinear Electrodynamic

evidence.text: How do nonlinear electromagnetic interactions modify electrically and magnetically charged black holes, including their geometry, thermodynamics, geodesics, regularity, holographic applications, and proposed quantum-gravity constraints?

sources.title: Extremalization approach to black hole thermodynamics: perturbations around higher-derivative gravities

evidence.text: Can Euclidean-action extremalization compute first-order black-hole thermodynamic corrections around known higher-derivative gravity backgrounds, retaining exact dependence on their original couplings and correctly treating AdS boundary data?

sources.title: Duality-invariant higher-derivative corrections to charged stringy black holes

evidence.text: How do duality-invariant higher-derivative terms change the extremal charge-to-mass ratio and attractor entropy of two-dimensional charged heterotic black holes, and what interpretation is possible in relation to weak gravity?

sources.title: Higher Derivative Corrections to R-charged Black Holes: Boundary Counterterms and the Mass-Charge Relation

evidence.text: Construct local intrinsic-curvature counterterms. Use Hamilton–Jacobi counterterm results for the Gauss–Bonnet sector and asymptotic field redefinitions to rescale the two-derivative counterterms for the other sectors.

sources.title: Kerr-Newman Black Holes with String Corrections

evidence.text: Embeds an Einstein-Maxwell field strength into the supergravity fields with constant X, Aμ=0 and T± aligned with the Maxwell field. Separately checks the two- and four-derivative Einstein equations using four-dimensional self-duality identities.

sources.title: Leading higher-derivative corrections to Kerr geometry

evidence.text: A conformal gauge for the meridional metric simplifies the horizon location. The authors calculate Killing-horizon quantities, embed horizon and ergosphere sections isometrically in Euclidean three-space, and solve circular null-geodesic and null-normalization equations for parity-preserving photon rings.

sources.title: Higher derivative corrections to Kerr black hole thermodynamics

evidence.text: Use I = βG, G = M−TS−ΩHJ and the first law to differentiate thermodynamic quantities. A change-of-variables argument relates the fixed-(M,J) entropy correction to minus the higher-derivative Euclidean action evaluated on Kerr.

sources.title: T-duality equivalences beyond string theory

evidence.text: Corrected duality rules are obtained through the doubled-vielbein formulation of Double Field Theory, gauge fixing and order-(a,b) field redefinitions connecting DFT fields to the generalized Bergshoeff–de Roo fields.

sources.title: On the extremality bound of stringy black holes

evidence.text: Evaluate the ten-dimensional Wald formula, including contributions induced by the Lorentz Chern–Simons term in the Kalb–Ramond field strength. The horizon binormal is normalized to εab εab = −2.

sources.title: Corrections to extremal black holes from Iyer-Wald formalism

evidence.text: How do arbitrary perturbations change four-dimensional Kerr-Newman extremality and entropy, and when can energy conditions constrain the sign of those changes without solving the corrected metric?

sources.title: Non-vanishing of tidal Love numbers

evidence.text: Does a cubic Riemann-curvature correction generate nonzero static black-hole tidal Love numbers, and can its correction to Wald entropy yield a controlled restriction on the coupling's sign?

sources.title: Black holes in Lorentz-violating gravity: Thermodynamics, geometry, and particle dynamics

evidence.text: How do nonminimal Kalb–Ramond couplings alter black-hole extremality relations, thermodynamic and photon-sphere topology, thermodynamic curvature, and massive-particle trajectories?

sources.title: Effective geometrodynamics for renormalization-group improved black-hole spacetimes in spherical symmetry

evidence.text: Can RG-improved Schwarzschild geometries be embedded in covariant variational theories with second-order spherical field equations, and how do improvements performed on solutions, equations and actions differ?

sources.title: Slowly rotating and accelerating <math display="inline"><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></math>-corrected black holes in four and higher dimensions

evidence.text: Can field redefinitions make the first string-curvature corrections analytically tractable for regular dilatonic black holes, including static solutions in arbitrary dimension and slowly rotating or accelerating solutions in four dimensions?

sources.title: On Black Hole Temperature in Horndeski Gravity

evidence.text: Can the failure of the usual Wald entropy and first-law prescription for certain Horndeski black holes be resolved through graviton propagation and a modified temperature, without adding an ad hoc scalar charge?

sources.title: Higher order correction to the GHS string black hole

evidence.text: What is the leading α′ correction to the extremal magnetic GHS black hole's mass-charge relation, and how can it be extracted despite field-redefinition ambiguity in the higher-derivative effective action?

sources.title: Entropy Bounds on Effective Field Theory from Rotating Dyonic Black Holes

evidence.text: What field-basis invariant constraints on four-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell EFT follow from positive classical Wald-entropy corrections for thermodynamically stable rotating dyonic black holes, and how do these constraints affect extremality and black-hole decay?

sources.title: (Un)attractor black holes in higher derivative AdS gravity

evidence.text: How do Gauss–Bonnet corrections affect renormalized charges, thermodynamics and scalar attractor behavior of static charged AdS black holes, including extremal solutions?

sources.title: Exploring String Theory Solutions: Black hole thermodynamics with $\alpha'$ corrections and type II compactifications

evidence.text: How do higher-derivative corrections and gauge freedoms affect heterotic black-hole thermodynamics, and how do source localization, membrane instabilities and integral-cohomology torsion affect type II compactifications?

sources.title: Black Hole Thermodynamic Ensembles, Euclidean Action and Legendre Transformation

evidence.text: Which black-hole ensembles can be obtained consistently by Legendre-transforming the Euclidean on-shell action, and how can geometric charges and Chern-Simons terms be accommodated while preserving agreement with the variational principle and Wald first law?

sources.title: Higher-Derivative Corrections to Entropy and the Weak Gravity Conjecture in Anti-de Sitter Space

evidence.text: How do four-derivative interactions change AdS-Reissner-Nordström extremality and microcanonical entropy, and what Wilson-coefficient constraints follow if entropy corrections are positive for thermodynamically stable black holes?

sources.title: Derivative corrections to extremal black holes with moduli

evidence.text: How do higher-derivative operators change the fixed-charge mass, entropy and long-range self-force of large extremal black holes with moduli, and are the three corrections correlated in ways relevant to the WGC and RFC?

sources.title: First order corrections to black hole thermodynamics: A simple approach enhanced

evidence.text: How can first-order higher-derivative corrections to black-hole thermodynamics be obtained without solving the perturbed metric when the correction changes the effective AdS cosmological constant?

sources.title: Black hole singularity resolution in <math display="inline"><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> via duality-invariant <math display="inline"><msup><mi>α</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></math> corrections

evidence.text: Can classical, duality-invariant corrections to all orders in α′ resolve the two-dimensional black-hole singularity while retaining a regular event horizon, and which choices of corrections admit such geometries?

sources.title: Fundamental Strings and Higher Derivative Corrections to d-Dimensional Black Holes

evidence.text: What are the leading α′ corrections to d-dimensional black holes carrying fundamental-string momentum and winding charges, and how do those corrections affect gravitational thermodynamics, entropy and mass/charge relations?

sources.title: Higher-Curvature Gravity, Black Holes and Holography

evidence.text: Which higher-curvature gravities have tractable linearized spectra and black holes, how do their corrections affect four-dimensional black-hole thermodynamics, and what CFT information can their AdS solutions reveal?

sources.title: Extremal Kerr Black Holes as Amplifiers of New Physics

evidence.text: Can small higher-curvature corrections produce large physical effects at extremal or near-extremal black-hole horizons despite small ambient curvature?

sources.title: De-singularizing the extremal GMGHS black hole via higher derivatives corrections

evidence.text: Can the fully nonlinear equations of an action truncated to O(α′) corrections resolve the singular extremal GMGHS horizon and admit regular, asymptotically flat bulk black holes?

destination.title: Axion dark matter: abundance and structure
destination.question: How do axion potentials, production histories and nonlinear evolution determine dark-matter abundance and gravitational signatures?
destination.summary: Connects relic production to later structure while preserving QCD, ultralight, fractional-abundance and nonlinear-collapse distinctions.

systems: QCD axions and axion-like dark matter
targets: Axion stars, minihalos and pressure-driven metric signals
assumptions: All-dark-matter and fractional-dark-matter hypotheses are source-specific.
Pure-glue calculations and axinova initial conditions are restricted inputs.
conventions: A decay-constant window alone does not establish a relic abundance.
excludes: Identifying a final vector relic as axion dark matter

sources.title: Dark Matter Axions Revisited

evidence.text: For which Peccei–Quinn scale fa, inflationary Hubble parameter HI and initial angle θi can invisible axions supply all cold dark matter, including corrections from potential anharmonicity?

sources.title: Quintessence Axion Revisited in Light of Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Could an electroweak axion with a potential scale different from the dark-energy scale serve as ultralight matter? The paper raises this possibility but does not identify a viable mass and abundance regime.

sources.title: Monodromy Dark Matter

evidence.text: Can axion monodromy relax the abundance restrictions linking misalignment-produced dark matter masses and couplings, and when do residual periodic wiggles change homogeneous evolution or amplify fluctuations?

sources.title: Impact of First-order Electroweak Phase Transition on QCD Axion

evidence.text: Can a temporary axion-mass contribution associated with a first-order electroweak transition change misalignment dynamics enough to obtain QCD-axion dark matter over a wider decay-constant range, while producing a potentially detectable gravitational-wave signal?

sources.title: Dark Matter Axions Revisited

evidence.text: Average θi²f(θi) uniformly over [−π,π] after inflation, obtaining 8.77 with the adopted anharmonic factor. During inflation use a single background angle plus variance σθ²=(HI/(2πfa))².

sources.title: Monodromy Dark Matter

evidence.text: Represent fluctuations by a Gaussian ensemble with spectrum P(k), and estimate position-space variance growth through momentum integration. The authors numerically find the variance difference finite even where the initial variance diverges; its late-time growth is dominated by the largest exponent.

sources.title: Quintessence Axion Revisited in Light of Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: The source evolves inverse gauge couplings piecewise across specified heavy thresholds. Only the caption and prose were available; the plotted curves, axis ticks, and numerical integration were not independently inspected or reproduced.

sources.title: Impact of First-order Electroweak Phase Transition on QCD Axion

evidence.text: The homogeneous axion equation θ̈+3Hθ̇+ma²(T)sinθ=0 is solved numerically across the three thermal phases, passing θ and θ̇ between phases. The kinetic and potential energy at TQCD is then redshifted to estimate the present relic density.

sources.title: Dark Matter Axions Revisited

evidence.text: Estimate oscillation onset using radiation-era Friedmann expansion, then evolve the misalignment abundance through conservation of comoving axion number relative to entropy.

sources.title: Monodromy Dark Matter

evidence.text: Numerically evolve the homogeneous field, then insert that background into linear Fourier-mode equations and extract momentum-dependent exponential growth rates. The numerical examples take vanishing initial background velocity.

sources.title: Relic Abundance of Dark Photon Dark Matter

evidence.text: Can energy initially stored in a misaligned axion produce the observed abundance of very light massive-vector dark matter through tachyonic amplification, including masses far below those efficiently populated by inflationary fluctuations?

sources.title: Dark Photon Dark Matter Produced by Axion Oscillations

evidence.text: Can coherent axion oscillations produce cold dark-photon dark matter through a tachyonic instability while visible-sector interactions eliminate the residual axion without violating cosmological constraints?

sources.title: Lattice QCD and Axion Cosmology

evidence.text: How can the finite-temperature topological susceptibility constrain the cosmological axion abundance and present-day axion mass, and what experimental guidance can a preliminary pure-glue lattice calculation provide?

sources.title: Recurrent axion stars collapse with dark radiation emission and their cosmological constraints

evidence.text: Can repeated formation, growth, and collapse of axion stars in dense minihalos convert enough cold dark matter into relativistic axions to constrain axion mass and attractive self-coupling independently of Standard Model couplings?
